title: Restore the isForbiddenRequestError export and cut pantheon-base-v0.18.1 as a consumer build fix
goal: Rebuilding pantheon-ops against pantheon-base-v0.18.0 failed in the consumer's own frontend code with TS2614: module ../../../../api/request has no exported member isForbiddenRequestError. The S1 unexport wave (#439, b0a1952a) removed that predicate on a zero-caller reading that covered only this repository, but api/request is a foundation surface that pantheon-ops imports (business/deploy/task/DeployTaskDetail.tsx:29, used at line 182). This package restores the two-line export, registers FR-021 and the section 5.4 rule about workspace-wide consumer reference searches, and cuts pantheon-base-v0.18.1 (patch, release/0.18) so the consumer can move off v0.18.0 and build both backend and frontend against the release that carries the thirteen simplification waves.
findings: frontend/src/api/request.ts in v0.18.0 does not export isForbiddenRequestError; pantheon-ops imports it and branches on it, so the consumer frontend build fails with TS2614 at DeployTaskDetail.tsx:29.
The removal came from S1 wave #439 (b0a1952a), whose zero-caller search was repository-local; api/request is a shared foundation surface, so caller enumeration has to span the workspace.

The v0.18.0 packet claimed both repository builds were green during the S1 wave; that reading did not cover the consumer tree, so the release shipped a surface that one consumer cannot compile against.
A patch is the honest level per docs/VERSION_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.md section 2.3: two restored export lines, no API, schema, route, permission, menu or i18n change.
This workstation intermittently times out on github.com:443 while api.github.com answers normally, so git fetch/push and release publication may need retries.

implementationNotes: The restore is deliberately two lines, not a wider API-surface review: three of the four request-error predicates were still exported, and a workspace reference search shows isForbiddenRequestError is the only api/request symbol pantheon-ops imports that was missing.
The consumer staging tree is the reproduction: build fails against v0.18.0 with TS2614, and passes when the export is restored, which is why the fix lands in base rather than as a consumer patch.

Section 5.4 records the rule the miss violated: removing a shared export requires a workspace-wide consumer reference search, and a foundation release is not verified until the consumer builds against it.
Publication preconditions are enforced by publish-foundation-release.mjs: clean worktree and a successful Release Gate Summary check on the target commit.
pantheon-ops already carries the 0.18.0 lock; this package advances it to 0.18.1 and records the diff rather than rewriting it.

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Restore exactly the export the consumer imports, then record the reproduction and the release mechanics; no wider API-surface redesign and no consumer-side workaround.

Confirm no workflow, gate or backend file appears in the diff.
